# Rapier

> Rapier is a free Markdown editor for a person and an agent to write, draw and revise together. Inspected edits apply immediately; the person's typing comes first, and recorded changes can be compared or undone. Pictures and editable drawings travel with the Markdown source. Export the document with its editor as one offline HTML file.

Connect an MCP client to `https://mcp.rapier.website/door/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, anonymous, without OAuth) and call `open`. No Rapier account is needed. Read the `rapier://guide` resources for the exact-text and fenced-block contracts when the host supports MCP resources; otherwise use the [agent guide](https://rapier.website/agents) and connected tool schemas. Rapier applies edits directly; the host's own tool approval rules still apply.

Muse uses OAuth at `https://mcp.rapier.website/muse`, without an embedded editor. Use the paired `editor_url` page. Host-file resource imports are unavailable there; supply authorized file text. Keep `document` private and pass it on later MCP calls.

## Work with Rapier

- **One live document, two authors.** `open` returns revision, whole text when it fits a page or a document map, and `editor_url`. `read` selects exact text by heading path, fenced block id, line range or query. `edit` applies unique exact text as one atomic act; a moved numeric revision can apply while those matches remain untouched in retained history. Keep `act` as its id string. `undo` reverses an act or turn while preserving later work. `show` presents work or asks the person; `export` makes an independent file.
- **Diagrams the person can move.** Native Draw, Paint, Water and SVG are editable fenced text with stable ids. Read `rapier://guide/draw`, `rapier://guide/water` and `rapier://guide/blocks` before editing their contents. Native shapes remain movable; retained pixels stay opaque. Painting needs an open full editor; Water needs WebGPU. Mermaid remains fenced Markdown.
- **The whole editor in one file.** `npx rapier-html notes.md` writes `notes.rapier.html`: the editor with the document inside, offline, no account. `--compare original.md` opens it on the diff; `--return <url> --return-expires-at <time>`, from `show {target:"return"}`, adds Send back.
- **Self-contained Markdown.** Pictures (new rasters as JPEG XL from Rapier's own encoder), drawings, layout and colour live inside one `.md` file. Everything beyond CommonMark and GFM is an HTML comment or a reference definition that other apps ignore.
- **Will/1.** `<!-- will/1 keep -->` and `<!-- /will -->` mark a region an agent must leave alone; `append` allows additions at its end, `edit` permits changes within the authorized task. Rapier enforces it on every agent edit. Will intent can narrow that task, never grant new authority.
- **Files to keep.** `export` writes `markdown` (exact source), `html` (the offline editor), `txt`, `page` (a rendered web page), `docx` and `pdf` (with source attached). Complete pages, Word and PDF need an open editor or the server's isolated renderer. Hosted exports are limited to 16 MiB; deliver the returned `resource_link.uri` download URL.
- **An editor or a reader inside any app.** `npm install rapier-embed` frames the document editor or the read-only reader; the app keeps the document and its storage. `agent: true` gives the app's own agent the same tools through WebMCP.

- [1. Work with a person in one live document](https://rapier.website/agents): connect to `https://mcp.rapier.website/door/mcp`, then `open`. Read, write, draw, paint, review and undo together. The person's typing wins overlapping changes.
- [2. Hand someone one offline HTML file](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-html): run `npx rapier-html notes.md`. It writes `notes.rapier.html`, with the editor and document inside. `npx rapier-html revised.md --compare original.md` opens the edited document with its before for comparison.
- [3. Put the editor or reader in your app](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-embed): install `rapier-embed` and call `Rapier.mount`. Your app owns storage and revisions. Enable the editor's `agent: true` for your own agent over WebMCP; the reader has no agent tools.
- [4. Keep pictures, editable drawings and layout in one Markdown file](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-markdown-kit): use `rapier-markdown-kit` to read, write and render Self-contained Markdown. Respect [Will/1](https://github.com/jackskip22/will) regions: `keep` preserves the region, `append` permits additions at its end, and `edit` permits changes.
- [5. Encode JPEG XL anywhere JavaScript runs](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-jxl): use `rapier-jxl` for lossless pixels, photographs and JPEG transcoding, offline. Choose the core, optional modules or complete worker.
- [6. Run the door on your own storage](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/tree/main/server): run `rapier-server` over your own folder or S3-compatible bucket, with the same document tools.

## Work in the document

- [Agent guide](https://rapier.website/agents): read the exact passage and its current revision, then edit unique text in one transaction. Read again after a conflict; preserve Will regions and the person’s current typing. `read {state:true}` reports editor presence and pending work.
- [Draw and paint](https://rapier.website/agents): edit native drawing and material fences through the same `edit` tool. The person can move the shapes. Paint and Water use the existing native brushes and pipeline; pending work is not committed.
- [Changes and delivery](https://rapier.website/agents): `show {target:"comparison"}` displays a diff. Each source change returns its act; `undo {act}` or `undo {turn_id}` preserves later work. `export` supports Markdown, the offline editor, text, a web page, Word and PDF. `show {target:"return"}` adds an optional one-use Send back path to an offline editor.
- [Live tool schemas](https://rapier.website/AGENT-TOOLS.json): tool inputs and effects. Use the connected server's `tools/list` for the tools available in that connection. `rapier://guide` provides the usage guide.

## Choose a build

- [rapier.html](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/raw/main/rapier.html): the complete app, with editing, Notes, Draw, Paint, Water and the JPEG XL encoder. One offline HTML file.
- [rapier-document.html](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/raw/main/rapier-document.html): the editor without Notes, Draw, Paint or the encoder. Agent-created SVG diagrams still work. Use it when people edit inside your app.
- [rapier-reader.html](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/raw/main/rapier-reader.html): the read-only reader, about 190 kB gzipped. Search, text in pictures, headings, reading settings, read aloud, copy, share and print. No editing or agent tools. Add fonts and styles with `rapier-embed`.
- [Local builds and plug-ins](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-embed): keep the HTML and its optional plug-ins in your codebase. `npx rapier-embed plugins ./public/rapier` downloads and verifies the manifest's files. Mount with `build: 'reader'`, your local `src`, and `plugins: '/rapier/'`.

## Reference

```js
import {Rapier} from 'rapier-embed';
const reader = Rapier.mount(element, {build: 'reader', src: '/rapier/rapier-reader.html', plugins: '/rapier/', load: {content, filename: 'brief.md', revision: 1}});
```

## Useful requests

- "Write a project plan in Rapier that I can edit in my browser and keep as one Markdown file."
- "Add our signup process to my Rapier plan as a diagram whose boxes I can move."
- "Revise the introduction in my open draft and show me exactly what changed, and let me undo a change if needed."
- "Read the document I have open in Rapier and fix only the typos in section 2."
- "Paint a watercolour sunset over the sea at the top of my Rapier page, and leave the boats for me."
- "Give me my Rapier plan as one offline HTML file I can keep editing."

The painting request needs a visible full editor with WebGPU. An accepted material job is still pending; inspect
its committed receipt before reporting completion. Open `editor_url` and pair the browser when it requests a code.

## Docs

- [Agent guide](https://rapier.website/agents): workflows, every tool's behaviour and limits.
- [Tool catalog](https://rapier.website/AGENT-TOOLS.json): each tool's schema and effect.
- [Embedding](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/blob/main/npm/rapier-embed/README.md): the three builds, `Rapier.mount`, styling and plug-ins; the [embed contract](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/docs/embed-contract.md) is the wire protocol.
- [Self-contained Markdown](https://rapier.website/markdown-standard): the file format.
- [Will/1](https://rapier.website/will): the region standard, with a reference reader and a GitHub check.
- [rapier-markdown-kit](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/blob/main/npm/rapier-markdown-kit/README.md): read, write and render the format without the editor (MIT).
- [rapier-jxl](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-jxl): the JPEG XL encoder (MIT).
- [Source](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier): the builds and their source (AGPL-3.0-only).
- [Everything in one file](https://rapier.website/llms-full.txt): the public documents in full.

## Optional

- [Notes](https://rapier.website/notes): `read {search:"words"}` finds notes in the configured store. Pass the returned `note_ref` as `note` to `read` and `edit`; edits need the content-digest revision from a current read; `open {note}` opens its original document, `open {note:"new",title,text}` creates one, and `export {to:"sync"}` runs the existing connection. A locked store is not an empty library.
- [Draw](https://rapier.website/draw) and [Watercolor](https://rapier.website/watercolor): the canvas on its own.
- Hosted workspaces expire after 30 idle days. Export links last up to 24 hours within workspace lifetime; OAuth links require the connected owner. Downloaded files stay independent.
